hints: Focus on the two separate test results, each one tells you about a different functional group feature.
Remember that fizzing with sodium to give hydrogen means an O-H group is present, so think alcohol or carboxylic acid here.
Now use the negative iodoform test to decide which alcohol fits, only molecules with $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ give the yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate.
walkthrough:
**Decode the sodium test**

Think of sodium as an O-H detector. Alcohols (and carboxylic acids and phenols) react to release hydrogen gas, which burns with a pop.

Chemical rule:
$$2\text{ROH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{RONa} + \text{H}_2$$

**Decode the iodine test**

Alkaline aqueous iodine is the iodoform test. A yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ forms only if the molecule contains a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group (in alcohols) or a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group (in carbonyls).

Our unknown does NOT give this precipitate, so it must NOT contain either of those groups.

**Test the four candidates**

Propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, and propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, have no O-H group, so they cannot give $\text{H}_2$ with sodium. They are out.

Both propan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, and propan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, give $\text{H}_2$ with sodium. But propan-2-ol contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ and would give a positive yellow precipitate. Only propan-1-ol fits both clues.

options.A: Propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, is an aldehyde with no O-H bond, so it does not react with sodium to give hydrogen. It correctly gives no yellow precipitate, but it fails the first test.
options.B: Propan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, has an O-H group so it reacts with sodium to give combustible $\text{H}_2$. Its structure is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-$ attached to $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, not $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so it gives a negative iodoform test. It fits both observations.
options.C: Propan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, does react with sodium to give $\text{H}_2$, but it contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group. It therefore gives a positive iodoform test with yellow $\text{CHI}_3$, so it fails the second condition.
options.D: Propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, is a ketone with no O-H bond, so it does not give hydrogen with sodium. It also contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ so it would give a yellow precipitate, failing both conditions.
